questions.question: Electromagnetic induction produces an emf whenever:
options: A coil carries a steady current
The magnetic flux through a coil changes
A magnet lies motionless beside a coil

questions.question: In an AC generator, the slip rings and brushes together:
options: Reverse the current every half turn
Step the voltage up for transmission
Connect the spinning coil to the external circuit while letting it rotate freely

questions.question: The output of a coil rotating between magnet poles is alternating because:
options: The magnetic field switches on and off
Each coil side sweeps up through the field for half a turn and down for the other half, reversing the induced emf

questions.question: Replacing the two slip rings with a split-ring commutator changes the generator's output to:
options: Direct current — pulsing in size but never reversing direction

questions.question: The motor effect is the observation that:
options: A spinning coil induces an emf
A current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field experiences a force

questions.question: A current-carrying coil in a field turns because:
options: Both sides are pushed in the same direction
The field pulls the whole coil toward one pole
Its two long sides carry current in opposite directions, so one is forced up and the other down

questions.question: Without a commutator, a DC motor's coil would:
options: Swing about half a turn and rock to a halt as the forces began acting backwards

questions.question: The statement that captures the generator-motor relationship is:
options: They are the same device operating in opposite energy directions

subtopics.title: Why the Grid Chose Alternating Current

questions.question: The decisive advantage of AC for a national grid is that:
options: Its voltage is easily stepped up and down by transformers, which need a changing current
AC needs thinner cables at the same current

questions.question: Power wasted as heat in a transmission line is given by:
options: I²R — it depends on the square of the current

questions.question: Transmitting a fixed amount of power at a very high voltage reduces losses because:
options: The same power then rides on a small current, and a small current squared is a tiny loss

questions.question: On a voltage-time graph of the mains, the negative half of each cycle represents:
options: Energy flowing back to the power station
The current flowing the opposite way around the circuit

questions.question: The rms value of an alternating voltage is defined as:
options: The plain average of the wave, which is zero
The equivalent DC value that would deliver the same average power to a resistor

questions.question: For the sine-wave mains, V max and V rms are related by:
A 55 Ω oven element on the 220 V mains carries an rms current and average power of:
The instantaneous power at the crest of the cycle, compared with the average power, is:
options: Double — average power equals half of V max times I max

subtopics.title: The Dynamo on the Bicycle Wheel

questions.question: A magnet lying motionless beside a coil for a hundred years produces:
options: Nothing — only changing flux induces an emf

questions.question: Pedalling becomes noticeably harder when the dynamo is engaged because:
options: The rider's extra mechanical work is what becomes the lamp's electrical energy
The magnet gains mass while spinning

questions.question: A power station generator differs from a bicycle dynamo mainly in:
options: Scale and what does the turning — the physics is identical

questions.question: Flicking a fan's blades by hand while a meter is connected across its plug makes the meter twitch because:
options: Static electricity builds on the blades
The spinning coil now acts as a generator — same parts, reversed energy flow

questions.question: The split ring in a DC motor swaps the current direction:
options: Every half revolution, timed to the coil passing vertical, so the push keeps the same rotational direction

questions.question: During regenerative braking, an electric vehicle's machine is acting as:
options: A generator — the rolling wheels spin the coil and push charge back into the battery
A resistor burning the energy as heat

questions.question: What decides whether the machine behaves as motor or generator is:
options: The direction of energy flow — which end you feed

questions.question: The mains voltage labelled 220 V actually peaks at about:
The plain time-average of the mains voltage wave is useless as a rating because:
options: It equals zero — the wave is negative as often as positive
It is too large to print on labels

questions.question: Heating happens on BOTH strokes of the alternating current because:
options: The wires store heat between strokes
Heat depends on current squared, which is positive in both directions
The negative stroke carries no energy

questions.question: An 1100 W heater on the 220 V mains draws an rms current of 5 A, but the wiring must be rated for:
options: The peaks near 7 A that occur twice each cycle
